reason: In PATO, the rolled-margin terms (involute PATO_0001962, revolute PATO_0001963 and convolute PATO_0001966) all sit under curled. Bare 'rolled' does not say which direction, so it goes to their parent. 'Rolled when dry' is handled by the specimen-condition pattern (06).
'Sub-' means 'nearly', which pattern 01 covers, and here it modifies the existing FLOPO equal. 'Subequal to perigynia' is a comparison with another part and goes to pattern 10.
This is 'nearly entire': the approximate-value pattern applied to the existing PATO entire.

Flowers 'in glomerules' are flowers in dense clusters, and PATO aggregated has the synonyms clumped and clustered. FLOPO capitate already sits under it. PO uses 'glomerule' for the compound capitulum of the Asteraceae, which is a different sense, so it is not used as the bearer here.
Semiterete means rounded on one side and flat on the other, which is the definition of FLOPO plano-convex. It is not a kind of PATO terete, which is round in section.
A broadly acute apex is still acute, only with a wider angle. 'Broadly' is a degree modifier that is not kept, as with other modifiers of width.

PATO shriveled means smaller and contracted, especially from loss of moisture, which is what 'withered' means. 'Withered at anthesis' is handled by the stage pattern. Withered but persistent parts are FLOPO marcescent (FLOPO:0991181) only when the source says they persist.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: obovate PATO_0001936 – elliptic PATO_0000947)
reason: This joins two existing shape values. It is a shape between the two, so it is handled as a continuum, like 'linear-lanceolate'.

The word is used in two senses: the chambered pith of Juglans, and lamellae as ridges on a labellum, disc or costa. 'Lamella' in the second sense is a generic part with no PO class. The chambered-pith sense could get its own term later from a cleaner sample.
PATO increased thickness has 'thickened' as a synonym, so 'not thickened' is its negation.
'Scales, pulp or paraphyllia abundant' means present in large numbers or amount. This follows the earlier rules that mapped 'tall' and 'enlarged' to PATO 'increased' terms.
Flaccid means limp and not rigid. Floras set it against 'rigid', which the earlier review mapped to PATO inflexible, so flaccid takes the opposite term.
This is a vague degree word whose meaning changes with context: 'present', 'prominent' or 'not reduced'. On its own it states no single quality.

label: proliferous
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's producing buds, shoots or plantlets from which new plants arise vegetatively. NOTE: Botany-specific (includes pseudoviviparous spikelets and root-suckering roots); PATO:0002102 proliferative is a cell-division quality.
reason: This is a real botanical character found on roots, spikelets and rachises. The structure it produces varies (bud, bulbil, plantlet), so a single presence rule cannot cover it.

label: bipinnatifid
definition: A pinnatifid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's pinnatifid lobes being themselves pinnatifid. NOTE: Follows FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate; sibling of FLOPO:0991155 pinnatisect.
reason: This is a standard term for how deeply a leaf is cut, and FLOPO only has the single-level pinnatifid.

label: pustulate
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing small, rounded, blister-like elevations, often at the bases of hairs. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991060 tuberculate; smaller than FLOPO:0991122 bullate; not PATO:0001928 blistered, which is an accumulation of fluid.
reason: This surface character is used widely (Boraginaceae hair bases, Begonia leaves). PATO blistered describes damage, and FLOPO bullate describes larger swellings between the veins.
PATO clasping means at least partly enclosing the axis, which covers half-clasping bases. The fully clasping case stays FLOPO amplexicaul.
A stem, stolon or node that is 'rooting' bears roots from the shoot, and 'adventitious root' is a synonym of PO shoot-borne root. 'Not rooting' is the absence.
A vaginate petiole base or stipule forms a sheath round the axis, which is what FLOPO sheathing means.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: margin + scarious FLOPO:0991047)
reason: The quality is scarious, and it applies to the margin of the named part. The region pattern covers this, so no new term is needed.

label: doubly serrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's marginal teeth bearing smaller teeth on their own margins. NOTE: Child of PATO:0001206 serrated; sibling of FLOPO:0991081 serrulate.
reason: This margin character is important for identification (Betula, Ulmus, Rosaceae), and neither PATO nor FLOPO has a term for it.
The PATO lexicon lists 'chestnut-brown' as a synonym of chestnut colour. The local quality.obo predates this term, so it should be updated.

target: docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md (sub- + parallel to PATO_0002272, among parts of the same kind)
reason: This is 'nearly parallel' between veins of the same order. Pattern 01 handles 'nearly', and the relation is among members of the same set. When the source names 'leaf blade' as the bearer, parallelodromous (PATO_0001968) would be the reading for the whole leaf.
An excentric midrib, style or tube is one that is not in the centre of its bearer, which is the negation of PATO centered.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: elliptic PATO_0000947 – lanceolate PATO_0001877)
reason: This joins two existing shape values to describe an in-between shape, so it is a continuum, like 'linear-lanceolate'.
This is the same case as 'covered' (rule C240): the word needs to say what covers the part. The quality lies in the sheaths or remnants that do the covering, not in the word 'clothed'.
Semiglobose means half a sphere, which is the definition of PATO hemispheroid.
Lignified or lignescent stems and rhizomes are woody, and PATO ligneous means resembling wood. 'Becoming lignified' is handled by the stage pattern.
This is the unhyphenated form of 'depressed-globose', which already has a rule (C170) mapping it to PATO oblate.
PATO elliptic is a 3-D (spheroid) shape with the synonym 'ellipsoid'. 'Broadly' is a degree modifier and is not kept, as with 'broadly acute'.
